claim.value: Increasing delay duration is a temporal pattern to seek.
claim.scope: A prospective observation category, not an observed trend.

provenance.rationale: The cited spans explicitly identify increasing delay duration as a pattern to seek and clarify that it is not an obtained finding.

signal_basis.value: Comparable recording of successive turnarounds and daily review with weekly summaries of delay minutes provide a sequence in which increasing delay duration can be sought.
signal_basis.scope: Prospective monitoring during the two-week investigation; observed patterns remain vulnerable to measurement errors, missingness and changing conditions.

provenance.rationale: The bundle supplies comparable sequential recording, delay-minute summaries, the prospective pattern category and its measurement limitations; P005 supplies the investigation timeframe.
No unresolved empirical relation is needed to license this prospective observation category.

rationale: Increasing duration is a temporal pattern that comparable repeated delay measurements can reveal. The claim merely identifies that pattern as something to seek, so the described operation licenses it without establishing an actual trend or its cause.
uncertainty: Whether an increase occurs or reflects underlying deterioration remains unresolved, but neither is asserted by this claim.
